page: Amazon Web Services r4.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the Xen hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The hardware allocation delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, FMA, BMI2, and AES, while newer vector formats such as AVX-512 are unsupported.

System memory totals 61.0 GB, providing an allocation of 7.62 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for file systems. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Hardware accelerators such as dedicated GPUs are absent.

Benchmark results reflect the legacy nature of the Broadwell-era processor architecture. Computational throughput tests report a stress-ng single-core score of 883.89 and a multi-core score of 4154.8, aligning with the bottom quartile of performance. Geekbench scores show 880.0 for single-core and 3333.0 for multi-core compute. Memory benchmarks demonstrate reasonable uncached large-block read bandwidth at 41.57 GB/sec, corresponding to an average PassMark memory score of 2184.03. In-memory data store tests register 2.32 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the r4.2xlarge lies in its high memory density against comparatively low single-thread and multi-thread processing power. Because modern instruction extensions and high baseline networking are omitted, the instance offers cost efficiency specifically when workloads are bottlenecked by RAM footprint rather than compute capacity. It functions best for in-memory caching systems, legacy memory-bound enterprise applications, medium-scale relational databases, and batch data transformation tasks.
